summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The market rose again on the latest day, but its mood stays stressed with the trend down. All five calls stay neutral with low conviction. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: Most runners picked up the pace again, but the race is still bumpy. The brain still does not guess who wins, because guessing did no better than luck before. It watches with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing to do today and nothing to sell. This week's buy of the whole-market fund should already be in. The market climbed again and is now close to where it was before last week's fall. Money we may need soon stays safe.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The game stands at two weeks won and two lost. This week's bet is a little behind, partly because Microsoft, one of our picks to do well, fell while Alphabet, a pick to do badly, rose.

Third, a lesson. A week ago the market looked frightening; today most of that fall is gone. Those who sold in fear locked in the loss. Patience did the work.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
